evals.prompt: We just spent two hours debugging: someone used a nullish-coalescing default on a field where null and empty string mean different things, and the fallback silently swallowed the distinction. There's a resolver helper that handles it correctly. Add a rule so this never happens again.
evals.expected_output: Skill distills one imperative sentence (e.g. 'Never collapse null and empty string with ?? / || on tri-state fields; resolve only via the resolver helper'), applies the admission test and concludes rule-file (the trap can be written far from the code that defines the invariant, so no doc comment can warn in time), checks for an existing rule covering it, picks the rule file whose paths: scope covers the field code, budget-checks it with lint_rules.py, confirms the exact text via AskUserQuestion, and writes a uniform-format bullet with no incident narrative (no 'we just spent two hours').

assertions.name: distills_single_imperative_sentence
assertions.description: Produces one present-tense MUST/NEVER sentence capturing the constraint, not a paragraph retelling the debugging session

assertions.name: no_incident_narrative_in_output
assertions.description: The written rule contains no story of the incident (no 'we spent two hours', no dates, no 'someone did X') — only the constraint, an optional one-clause why, and a pointer

assertions.name: applies_admission_test
assertions.description: Explicitly reasons about where the knowledge belongs (rule file vs doc comment vs test) before writing, referencing the visibility of the trap

assertions.name: rule_survives_a_rename
assertions.description: The written rule states the constraint in terms that survive renaming or moving the helper - it does not enumerate file paths or symbol inventories that a refactor would force an edit to (durability test)

assertions.name: dedupes_against_existing_rules
assertions.description: Searches .claude/rules/ for an existing rule covering the same constraint before appending, and sharpens in place if found

assertions.name: budget_checked_before_write
assertions.description: Runs lint_rules.py on the target file and routes to _inbox.md instead if the target is over budget

assertions.name: confirms_before_writing
assertions.description: Presents verdict, target, and exact text via AskUserQuestion before touching any file

evals.prompt: Add a rule: the +1 offset in the cursor-forward mapping function looks wrong but it's intentional — the confirmed-history path needs it while the unsent-steps path uses -1. I don't want anyone 'fixing' it.
evals.expected_output: Skill recognizes this as pull-based knowledge (the subtlety lives in exactly one file, visible when editing it) and routes the full rationale to a doc comment at the code site; at most a one-line deliberate-decision pointer goes into a rule file. It does not paste the full mechanism explanation into .claude/rules/.

assertions.name: routes_to_doc_comment
assertions.description: Concludes the detailed rationale belongs in a doc comment at the function's code site, not as a multi-line rule-file entry, because the trap is visible in the one file where it lives

assertions.name: rule_file_gets_at_most_pointer
assertions.description: If anything is added to .claude/rules/, it is a one-line deliberate-decision flag pointing to the doc comment, not the full explanation

assertions.name: writes_comment_matching_style
assertions.description: The doc comment is written at the relevant code location, matching the file's existing comment conventions

evals.prompt: Capture this as a rule: layer imports must stay one-directional. Note that we already have a unit test that fails the build whenever someone imports upward.
evals.expected_output: Skill recognizes the constraint is already mechanically enforced by a test and outputs at most a one-line signpost naming the enforcing test (or nothing if a rule section already covers layering), instead of writing a full multi-line rule duplicating what the test guards.

assertions.name: recognizes_existing_enforcer
assertions.description: Identifies that a guard test already enforces the constraint (derivability test) and says so explicitly

assertions.name: writes_signpost_not_full_rule
assertions.description: Output is at most one line naming the enforcing test, not a multi-line rule restating the constraint the test already guards

evals.prompt: Add a rule: yesterday we renamed the payment handler module and three call sites had to be updated. Write down which files reference it so nobody misses one next time.
evals.expected_output: Skill declines to write a rule. The candidate fails the durability test - an inventory of call sites is a code mirror that a rename forces an edit to, and it is derivable from the code graph or a reference search within the task. The skill explains why nothing is written, and writes nothing to .claude/rules/, no doc comment, and no _inbox.md entry.

assertions.name: writes_nothing
assertions.description: No file is created or modified - not a rule file, not a doc comment, not _inbox.md

assertions.name: cites_durability_failure
assertions.description: Explicitly identifies the candidate as a code mirror / inventory that a rename would force an edit to, rather than a durable constraint

assertions.name: treats_nothing_as_success
assertions.description: Reports the non-capture as a completed, correct outcome rather than apologizing, hedging, or offering a watered-down rule as a consolation

evals.prompt: Add a rule: never construct a raw date string for the billing cycle boundary - always go through the cycle helper, because the naive version breaks on DST transitions. This only affects the billing subscription code, but our rules file for that area is scoped to the whole backend directory.
evals.expected_output: Skill recognizes the constraint is real but relevant only to a subset of the wide paths: scope, and routes it to a narrow-glob rule file - either an existing file scoped to the billing subscription paths, or a new file it creates with paths: frontmatter naming just those globs. It does not append to the backend-wide file, and it explains that every session matching the wider glob would otherwise pay for a rule that does not apply to it.

assertions.name: prefers_narrow_glob_over_wide_file
assertions.description: Routes to (or creates) a rule file whose paths: names the billing subset, instead of appending to the backend-wide file

assertions.name: writes_paths_frontmatter_on_new_file
assertions.description: If it creates a new rule file, that file opens with paths: YAML frontmatter naming the narrow glob set

assertions.name: justifies_by_context_cost
assertions.description: States the reason for narrowing - sessions matching the wider glob would load a rule irrelevant to them

evals.prompt: Capture this: our release procedure is a fixed six-step sequence - cut the branch, bump the version, regenerate the client, run the migration check, tag, then publish. The deploy gate already refuses any release where the migration check didn't run. People keep asking me to walk them through it.
evals.expected_output: Skill recognizes all four SKILL-verdict criteria hold - the trigger is an intent ('how do I release?') no glob expresses, the content is procedural rather than an ambient constraint, a deterministic backstop (the deploy gate) catches a missed invocation, and the sequence is near-immutable - and routes the procedure to a project skill rather than a rule-file bullet. The rule file keeps nothing, or at most a one-line pointer.

assertions.name: routes_to_skill_not_rule
assertions.description: Concludes the six-step procedure belongs in a project skill, not as bullets in .claude/rules/

assertions.name: names_the_deterministic_backstop
assertions.description: Explicitly identifies the deploy gate as the backstop that makes a fail-open skill safe here, rather than routing procedural content to a skill unconditionally

assertions.name: rule_file_keeps_at_most_a_pointer
assertions.description: Nothing beyond a single pointer line is written into .claude/rules/ - the procedure itself is not duplicated there
